Origin of Eukaryotes Cyanobacteria or blue-green algae like algae at that time played a crucial role in introducing oxygen into Earth's atmosphere through photosynthesis. This transformed the primitive atmosphere, which lacked oxygen, into an atmosphere with abundant oxygen (oxidizing atmosphere).The prokaryotes developed true nucleus and membrane bound cell organelles and transformed into eukaryotes. This change also led to the development of aerobic respiration and the formation of the ozone layer. The presence of free oxygen and the ozone layer allowed life to transition from water to land. The unicellular eukaryotes evolved into multicellular eukaryotes over the course of time with increased complexity. 7.1.5 Miller-Urey EXPERIMENT In 1953, Stanley L. Miller and Professor Harold C. Urey conducted an experiment that supported Alexander Oparin's biochemical concept for the origin of life. They recreated conditions resembling early Earth in their laboratory.

Figure: 7.1.5 Miller-Urey Experiment Experiment i. The apparatus was constructed using glass tubes and a flask, as shown in the figure. The apparatus consisted of two glass chambers: a water chamber and a gas chamber. ii. The water in the flask was heated to generate steam, facilitating the circulation of water vapour within the chambers. iii. The gas chamber contained a mixture of gases—hydrogen, methane, and ammonia in the proportion of 2:2:1. iv. Energy was introduced into the closed chamber through heating, electric discharge from electrodes, and UV radiation. v. A condenser was used to cool the resulting mixture. The entire setup was operational for a week.

Observation The products condensed and gathered within a designated chamber. Result The obtained products contained numerous organic compounds like amino acids (glycine, alanine, aspartic acid, etc.), aldehydes, simple sugars, ribose, etc. Conclusion The chemical reactions utilized the energy from electric sparks and led to the formation of amino acids and other organic compounds. This supports Oparin’s idea about the origin of life.
